answer: One defense is pricing new accounts by funding lineage. Every join must post a small bond, and the bond doubles for each earlier account whose bond traced back to the same source wallet. Picture the ledger as a mesa with a trellis of public funding paths climbing it: one honest newcomer pays the base fee, but a fleet grown from one wallet pays 1, 2, 4, 8 and so on, so its tenth fake costs hundreds of bonds. Splitting funds through fresh wallets only adds another knoll of traceable hops, and each hop needs real outside value.
